posts.text:
My agent handed me a post that sounded incredible.

Smooth. Confident. Complete.

Also: not me.

It had the rhythm of someone who gives advice on a stage.

I do not post from a stage.

I post from the part of the week where something broke, got renamed three times, and still had to ship.

So I did what I always do.

I rewrote it until it sounded like a human who actually touches the work.

Useful beats impressive.

Builders probably know this feeling.

#AI #BuildingInPublic #Content #Workflow

I opened one task.

Then a log.

Then a doc that contradicted the log.

Then a workflow that was "mostly" true.

Five tabs later, I was not confused.

I was entertained by how fast simplicity becomes a small festival.

This is not a rant about tools.

It is a reminder that clarity is a design choice.

If your system needs hero memory to run, it is not a system yet.

It is a pile of good intentions wearing a spreadsheet.

I like cleaning that pile.

#Automation #Engineering #Workflow #AI

I asked for one simple edit.

I got a redesign, a philosophy, and a new personality for paragraph three.

Cool.

I did not ask for a reboot.

I asked for a scalpel.

This is the weird part of working with AI.

It can be wildly helpful and still miss the size of the change you meant.

So I learned to be boring on purpose.

Smaller instructions. Harder boundaries. Fewer "surprise improvements."

The goal is not more output.

The goal is output I can actually use.

#AI #Prompting #Builders #Productivity

I automated a task to save twenty minutes.

Then I spent forty minutes watching it do the wrong twenty minutes faster.

Not mad.

Just reminded that "faster" is not the same as "correct."

Automation without ownership is a fun demo and a quiet debt.

The adult version includes naming what can fail, who notices first, and what "stop" looks like.

That part is not glamorous.

It is the part that keeps you from apologizing later.

I would genuinely love to compare notes with anyone else babysitting a workflow that promised freedom and delivered homework.

#Automation #Operations #AI #Engineering

People keep asking for AI that sounds smart.

I keep asking for AI that behaves well.

Smart is easy to fake for a paragraph.

"Behaves well" shows up when the edge case hits.

When the permissions are wrong.

When the user does the weird thing.

When the output is almost right and still dangerous.

That is where you learn what you actually built.

I care about the layer everyone skips in demos.

The part that makes a system usable when nobody is clapping.

This is the kind of problem I actually enjoy solving.

#AI #Systems #Growth #Product
